sentence: This project studies how the body's emergency blood cell production works and how it goes wrong in immune problems, solid cancers, and blood disorders.
This project uses gene editing in living animals to find out how macrophages and fibroblasts help lung cancer tumors grow.
This project builds a design method that finds the best shape for radiofrequency coils used in magnetic resonance imaging and tests it in simulations.
This project studies how a mouth bacterium and its large sticky protein change the way a gum disease bacterium settles on cells lining the mouth.
This project tests whether two types of nerve channels change how the surface of the eye makes mucins that protect the cornea from bacteria.
This project sets up a training program in cancer research that builds on strengths in DNA repair and epigenetics.
This project uses computer methods to study how enzymes carry out and control chemical reactions that are linked to human diseases.
This project tries to find out how human cells keep their mitochondria healthy and respond when mitochondria are under stress.
This project tries to find small molecules that control molting in parasitic nematodes, a process these worms need to develop.
This project studies how mutation, selection, and drift shape the structure and sequence of genomes over different timescales.
This project tries to find out how the nutrients in pancreatic tumors make cancer cells resist chemotherapy and whether changing them helps.
This project studies how mitochondrial electron transport shapes the metabolism and signaling of kidney epithelial cells.
This project improves a platform that captures single immune cells and reads their metabolites, lipids, glycans and proteins with mass spectrometry.
This project builds a blood test that detects misfolded proteins in a small plasma sample to find heart and blood diseases early.
This project builds a global online resource that lets researchers share, find and reuse proteomics mass spectrometry datasets.
This project builds computer methods that read single cells in images and a way to link genes to cell behavior through imaging.
This project studies how epigenetic states let a regulatory element act as an enhancer in one cell type and a silencer in another.
This project studies which patient and clinical factors could explain suicides that followed a prescription opioid change, using surveys, record review and interviews.
This project uses computer methods to study how enteroviruses infect cells, focusing on their capsids, proteins and membranes.
This project studies how human natural killer cells respond to Coccidioides, a fungus that can cause lung disease.
